steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: The auditorium is...

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Huh? Is this not the place?

steps.name: Enthusiastic Voice
steps.text: You're back too?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: The auditorium is this way. Follow me!

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: I came back as soon as I got word from the Messenger.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: So many people... it's like everybody's back...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: The internal layout is being continuously improved, but people still get lost all the time.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: We're going to put some signs up.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: I couldn't believe it when I first heard that HQ was being moved to a nomadic plate... didn't have the access level to find out what exactly happened in the incident.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: All I heard is something about Originium, and that the ship was abandoned and everyone was evacuated.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: No need to worry. Like the Doctor said, we'll dig the old ship out.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Uh-huh... I saw Amiya on my way here. I asked about Dr. Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: She didn't go into details, only told me not to worry—

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Before I got the chance to comfort her.
Red still harbors hope.
She is hiding in the shadows in a corner, the bag holding her baby tooth in her pocket.
Red wanted to sneak it into Kal'tsit's pocket when she came back, but it was someone else who did.
She wants to hear about Kal'tsit today. She knows that the Doctor and Mon3tr have been working on something in secret.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Uh... Dr. Warfarin? I thought it was the Doctor's presentation.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: No need to look so nervous.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: I'm simply here to give a talk on a paper. Medical Department's routine.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname} is currently busy with something else, and there is no one more suited than I.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: This paper was co-authored by one of my patients, by the name of Chloe.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: In the recent incident on Rhodes Island, she helped us complete a critical piece of Oripathy research.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Not only did this research turn the tides at the time, it also provides guidance for every medical worker with an interest in Oripathy moving forward.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Usually, this is the time when I talk about the authors, their biographies, their achievements...

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: When it comes to Chloe, however, I'm not sure where to start.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Her resume is largely a blank sheet. To be honest, I hardly took any interest in her past in the three years that I cared for her.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: I left only a few comments in her file—

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Oripathy patient from Victoria. Not always diligent about following doctor's instructions. Makes atrocious noises in the ward with her handmade clocks...

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: She was the one who proposed the key hypothesis of the experiment, and the one who provided a precious sample.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: The sample was herself.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: She asked me to harm her, in order to obtain more accurate data from the objective changes that occurred to her.
Few of the operators at the presentation have ever seen Dr. Warfarin so serious.
More than a few thought about sneaking out quietly at first, when they found out that she was the one presenting.
At the end, however, they all stayed, out of respect to Chloe's sacrifice, and because they all wanted to know what exactly happened to Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: As her doctor, I could not approve of her choice.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: As a member of Rhodes Island, however, I am indebted to her courage—

a.text: 'Her condition was unusual, special. Perhaps she had a chance to escape the despair of Oripathy, to live on in another way.'

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I-I've made my choice.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: You want to go back to the land that belonged to you?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: You know what this means. You will face death once again.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Death has always been the conclusion to life.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: In this place, I've seen so many 'gods' that I could not even fathom, and learned so much from them.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I want to go back and tell my people...

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: The end may be destined, but they need not live in fear of death and disintegration.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Perhaps I can soothe the fear that Originium brings them.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Is this all you want?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Yes.
The Cautus looks at Priestess with firm eyes. The miracle maker takes her hand.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Come with me, then.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: I will take you home.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Is there anything here that you will miss?
The Cautus shakes her head.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Will I ever see you again?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: I'm not a prophet. I can't see your future.
Priestess takes the Cautus's hand, and they walk into the shadow of the megastructure.
They walk towards the silent conclusion of countless civilizations, the cradle of new hope.

a.text: '...Our joint research has validated a key conclusion.'
'A change is occurring to Originium, the nature of which we have yet to ascertain. It has already had a chain effect on our patients.'
'We have empirically demonstrated the existence of new symptoms of Oripathy for the first time since the large-scale infection incident in Victoria three years ago.'
'This will take Terra's Oripathy research into a new direction. Whether this is for the better or for the worse remains to be seen, as we continue to accumulate case studies and data.'

steps.text: The Cautus smells wind and sand as her eyes adjust to the light.
There is no doubt about it. This is her Terra. She is home.
She can still feel the warmth in her hand, but she is alone.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: You're gone...

steps.name: Voice from Far Away
steps.text: I can't believe there's someone else in this forsaken place—

steps.name: Voice from Far Away
steps.text: ...seek help from her... she looks even weaker than us...

steps.name: Voice from Far Away
steps.text: I know it hurts... I'll find help... wait for me... hang in there...
The Cautus sees someone run towards her frantically.

steps.name: Miner
steps.text: H-Hello, could you contact the nearest hospital—no, it would be too late—

steps.name: Miner
steps.text: Would you happen to have any suppressants? It looks like you're Infected too...
The miner grabs Hierda's hand like a drowning man grasps at a straw.
She does not have any suppressants, nor does she know how to contact the nearest hospital.
But she does not want to take hope away from her brethren.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Is there any trouble? You can take me there.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Maybe I can help.
Maybe.

steps.name: Miner
steps.text: Thank you! Thank you so much!

steps.name: Miner
steps.text: My brother's over there!
Hierda is stunned by what she sees as they hurry around the hills.
A massive Originium crystal is stuck in between the walls of a vast canyon.
Hierda can see something sealed within the crystal.
A ship?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: What... is that?

steps.name: Miner
steps.text: We found a new vein here, and we wanted to give it a try before we registered it...

steps.name: Miner
steps.text: I mean, look at how rich the color is! Besides, there might be something even more valuable within...

steps.name: Miner
steps.text: But listen, there's something not right with this place! It's like someone's watching us, and my brother got infected from a wound he picked up in an accident—

steps.name: Infected Worker
steps.text: (Screams in pain)

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: It looks really bad. You know as well as I do that he's about to disintegrate... there's nothing that can be done.

steps.name: Miner
steps.text: I-I can't just leave him here. We have thirteen siblings waiting for us at home—

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Listen to me. Run, as far away as possible.

steps.name: Miner
steps.text: B-But...

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Don't look back. Run.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I've dealt with this before. Leave it to me.

steps.name: Infected Worker
steps.text: (Mumbles with great difficulty) Go...

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I understand your pain. I know the terror that overtakes us when the light fades from our eyes...

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I've been there.

steps.name: Infected Worker
steps.text: (Mutters in shock)

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: All I can do is walk with you to the end.
The Cautus holds the hardened hand of the dying, trying to give him one last sliver of warmth.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: May your pain be eased, even just a little.

steps.name: Infected Worker
steps.text: My pain... it-it's gone!
The Cautus does not understand what happened—The rocks are still spreading on the body of the dying.
But the color of the black rocks becomes increasingly pure, and they begin to glow orange.

steps.name: Infected Worker
steps.text: H-How did you do that?!

steps.name: Infected Worker
steps.text: They don't hurt any more. Why...?
The shocked man tries to move, and finds that movement comes naturally, as though the accident never happened.
Except for the Originium that continues to grow.
Perhaps there will come a day when it replaces his flesh and blood in its entirety.
What will become of him when that day comes?

steps.name: Infected Worker
steps.text: I feel myself recovering. This is amazing...

steps.name: Infected Worker
steps.text: H-Have I been freed from death?
He looks at the Cautus girl, only to see the same shocked expression in her eyes.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: —Did you grant my wish? Or is it...
She does not see the one she wants to see, but catches a glimpse of a figure on a distant peak, gazing at them.
The figure turns around and leaves.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: —This paper means a lot to me personally.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Chloe's efforts reminded me why Rhodes Island exists, and why Kal'tsit is committed to our path.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Unlike any period in its history, Rhodes Island today is not only a pharmaceutical company that fights the pain brought about by Oripathy—

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: It must deal with the Originium problem at the source too.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: We brought hope to those who had lost it. In turn, they repay us with hope.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: This paper is Rhodes Island's salute to Chloe, and a promise on our part—

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: —A promise to Kal'tsit.
You arrive after Warfarin's speech has concluded.

options: Thank you for doing the presentation on my behalf.
She was a patient who saved her doctor.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: You look happy. Are you done on your end?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Yes, Dr. Warfarin.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: With Mon3tr's help, we managed to identify some key pieces of information in the vast amounts of data that Dr. Kal'tsit left behind.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: You mean...?!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Dr. Warfarin! I found a way!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: My connection to her was severed, but her bio-identification signals and neuron data are still stored inside my brain.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Plus the neural network I had shared with her, in theory, all we'll need is a life support device powerful enough to—

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Slow down, slow down! What exactly are you getting at?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: What I mean is, although it's a purely theoretical possibility...

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: By using the power of the Sarcophagus...

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: We can bring Kal'tsit back!

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: I knew Kal'tsit wouldn't go so easily...

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: But the Sarcophagus? The one that was on Rhodes Island?

options: We can't go back to Rhodes Island for a while.
There is only one other Sarcophagus accessible to us.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It's like we've come full circle.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: This will not be easy. Ursus remains a dangerous place for Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: But Kal'tsit has planned ahead and made arrangements at all our branches across Terra. Our first priority should be to restore communications with them.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: We'll need their help for what we're trying to do.

options: We'll make contact with Ursus first.
Then, we'll find a way to bring Kal'tsit back.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: So this is what Terra looks like now.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: 'Kolossal Prime Vein'? That's what they're calling that piece of Originium these days?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Hmm. Maybe it'll be a good choice for the next step.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: The rate of Originium propagation is far below expected values, and AMa-10 has been a significant hindrance.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: The project must be accelerated. Time is short.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: The evolution of this planet is taking place too slowly.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: More radical means are called for—
She walks deeper into the Abyss, now sealed in Originium.

a.text: Error: Database missing. Search function unavailable.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: ...Looks like connection by PRTS won't be possible for now.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Perhaps—

a.text: You don't know what you're doing, Dr. {@nickname}...
It's unfortunate that you have forgotten everything, our explorations of space, the shared pins that anchor our thoughts, and the 'debate' that has lasted so many millennia...
And your very first promise to me...
Time, the most cruel of mazes. It leads us astray, and separates us from each other.
But I believe, I've always believed, that you will once again recognize the truth of this universe, and our inevitable end.
I believe that you will come back to me when that time comes.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: You've led us on a long walk, Sankta.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Have you decided to become a bounty hunter too?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: You talk too much, Sarkaz.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Your fate was sealed the moment you decided to attack that innocent Siracusan caravan.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: But it was too close to the Kazdelian border. His Holiness has encouraged upholding justice through proper means, to maintain peace on the surface, and it was not my place to go against the rules.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: This place will do.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: You're too far from home, mercenary.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: You should have stayed in Kazdel, and never came out of that pit of yours.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Hmph.
Oren raises his gun.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: ...You missed?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: You—you—

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: My hand should not be trembling.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Yes, you should fear me, Sarkaz. It's over.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Wait! Wait—

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: M-Monster! What are you?!
Oren takes a questioning look at his gun, and sees a shocking sight in the reflection of the gleaming metal.
His halo flashes frantically above his head.
Dazed and confused, he looks at his reflection again, and the devil that he is about to execute—
They look exactly the same.
